text: A doorway to another doorway. Build two stone frames, link their keystones, light one, and anything that walks in comes out of the other: players, animals, mobs and dropped items alike.
pages.title: Way Gate
Building the frame
pages.text: A five-by-five ring without its corners, keystone in the middle of the bottom row. The inside, three wide and three tall, stays empty.

pages.title: Frames and keystone
text: One craft of six March Stone, two copper and an Echo Shard makes **four Gate Frames**. A ring takes **11** frames, and the keystone itself takes four more, with a Resonant Core, a Spirit Shard and a Pulse Cell.

The keystone holds the gate's Pulse, up to **600**. Right-click it with a Pulse Cell to pour in up to **100** a time. A lit gate also tops itself up by up to 40 a second from generators within 8 blocks.
Only the player who placed a keystone, and their camp, can charge, light or break it.

pages.title: Linking a pair
text: Build the second gate within the same world.
- **Compass:** crouch and right-click the first keystone with an unbound Waystone Compass to bind it there, then crouch and right-click the second keystone with that compass.
- **Chalk:** right-click one keystone with Ritual Chalk, then the other, up to **64 blocks** apart.
- A Gate Sigil works too; see [Far Gate](far_gate).
The pair answers both ways. **/tribalpower gate list** names every pair.

pages.title: Lighting and crossing
text: Right-click the keystone with an empty hand to light it: **400 Pulse** from its store. Right-click again to let it go dark. A struck redstone signal toggles it the same way, while a held signal keeps it dark and refuses travel.

Each crossing takes **20 Pulse** from the gate you walk into. You land inside the partner's frame, lit or not. A **one-second** cooldown stops you bouncing straight back. Riders and vehicles cannot pass.
A comparator reads **0** unlinked, **1 to 14** for stored Pulse, and **15** as something crosses.
See [Keeping the way](keeping_the_way) for what happens when things go wrong.
